Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Iteration 1/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response

record.narrative: Critical appraisal: none of R1-R12 has a 95% Welch interval that excludes zero, so there is no discovery evidence sufficient to accept any of the pre-registered positive or negative associations. I therefore avoid claiming any effect in the supplied dataset. Using the observed outcome mean magnitude as an approximate clinical scale benchmark, the approximate 10% differences are about 0.0415 for outcome_001, 0.0175 for outcome_006, 0.0093 for outcome_014, 0.0301 for outcome_011, and 0.0282 for outcome_008. H1 and H4 are the cleanest null-equivalence results: for outcome_001, both exposure contrasts have intervals entirely inside the approximate +/-0.0415 clinical threshold, so I reject clinically meaningful differences for feature_034 and feature_002 on outcome_001. H8 is close to equivalence but is borderline because the lower limit is nearly at the outcome_008 threshold; given ambiguity in the exact comparator-relative benchmark and multiplicity, I leave it unresolved rather than assert equivalence. H3 and H7 have near-zero point estimates but outcome_014 has a small mean magnitude, so the clinical threshold is small and the intervals remain too wide to rule out clinically meaningful differences. H2 and H5 for outcome_006 also have intervals extending beyond the small clinical threshold, and H6 extends into a clinically meaningful positive direction. The interaction estimates are even more uncertain because they use median splits and four-cell contrasts. H10 is the most visually interesting discovery result: a signed interaction of -0.0432 is large relative to outcome_006 mean magnitude, but its interval -0.113 to +0.027 includes both null and clinically meaningful opposite-direction differences, and it is the largest among many exploratory subgroup contrasts. This is not compelling enough to validate. Overall, the evidence pattern is mostly null or imprecise, with no coherent strong effect modification signal. I request no independent validation now because the validation budget is better used later for a precise or replicated claim. The proposed follow-ups test two additional balanced binary predictors and convert the largest interaction lead into a direct subgroup mean effect for H10 while keeping the interpretation exploratory. No causal or generalizability claims are made.

number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

In this dataset only, the evidence does not support any positive or negative association claim among the first 12 registered comparisons. The two strongest supported conclusions are negative/equivalence-style: for outcome_001, both feature_034 and feature_002 show contrasts with 95% intervals entirely within the approximate 10% clinical-effect range, so I reject scientifically meaningful differences for those two specific tested contrasts. This allocation follows the current lead, broadens predictor coverage, and targets outcomes with clinically interpretable scale. If any next result has a signed point estimate beyond roughly the 10% relative threshold and an interval that mostly excludes null, I will accept it as a dataset-association and then consider independent validation. Otherwise, the investigation should be closed or deferred. These remain associations in the supplied data, not causal or generalizable claims.

No discovery interval excluded zero, and the strongest exploratory lead remained the feature_034 by high-feature_051 interaction for outcome_006, which is imprecise and not validation-ready. The next comparisons should therefore be chosen to improve power and clarify this lead. I propose extending the three near-balanced binary markers feature_034, feature_060, and feature_002 to outcomes with relatively favorable 10%-relative thresholds and adequate absolute variability: outcome_011, outcome_008, outcome_013, and outcome_001. These have larger detectable margins than outcome_014 and, for binary exposures with near-balanced groups, offer better precision. The new main-effect hypotheses retain a negative-association orientation: the exposed binary level is hypothesized to be associated with a more negative CRISPR dependency score, i.e., stronger dependency; direction is set to -1 so a positive signed estimate would support that negative raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast. Anticipated alternatives are no association, the opposite protective or lineage-defining direction, or an association confined to a subgroup. The direct low-feature_051 subgroup test for outcome_006 by feature_034 is a focused decomposition of the H10 interaction lead: if the H10 signal reflects a true subgroup effect, the exposed-versus-comparator contrast should be clearer in the high-feature_051 cell than in the low cell. The complementary low cell is expected to be null if the interaction is genuinely high-group-specific, but an opposite or similar low-group effect would change interpretation. To keep the next analysis set focused, I defer several currently active lower-prevalence or small-threshold claims, especially feature_045/feature_065/feature_021/feature_052 main effects and lower-information feature_054 outcomes, while keeping the H16 high-feature_051 direct contrast and the strongest feature_054 main effects active. These are associations in the supplied dataset only; causality and generalizability remain unassessed until precise interval results or independent validation are available.

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

record.narrative: Critical appraisal of the 12 new discovery results: I used an approximate clinical-effect scale of 10% of the absolute outcome mean because these dependency scores have negative means: outcome_001 about 0.0415, outcome_006 about 0.0175, outcome_008 about 0.0282, outcome_011 about 0.0301, and outcome_013 about 0.0269. The returned estimates are already signed to each claim direction. None of the intervals excludes zero, so I accept no positive or negative association claim from these 12 results. H16 is the most compelling direct follow-up to the earlier H10 interaction lead: in the high-feature_051 cell for outcome_006, the signed estimate is -0.0327 with interval -0.0817 to +0.0163. The point is roughly twice the clinical scale and the upper bound just excludes a clinically meaningful positive raw effect, but the negative direction is not established because zero remains inside the interval. I therefore keep H16 unresolved and active and request independent validation rather than accept it. H27 is a possible opposite-direction signal: under a negative-direction claim the signed estimate is -0.0187, meaning the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is positive; the raw interval allows a clinically meaningful positive difference but includes zero, so the original negative claim is unresolved and a positive-direction refinement is proposed. H17 and H20 show a consistent negative raw feature_054 contrast on outcome_001 and outcome_011, but neither point estimate is beyond the clinical threshold and both intervals include zero; these remain active but unresolved. H32 is a clean equivalence-style null: outcome_013 feature_002 signed +0.0036, interval -0.0163 to +0.0235, entirely inside the clinical margin, so I reject a clinically meaningful difference for that tested contrast. H14 is also mostly inside the clinical margin but borderline and low prevalence, so with multiple testing and scale ambiguity I defer rather than formally reject. H25, H26, H31, H15, H24, and H29 are weak or imprecise: intervals include zero and often extend beyond the clinical threshold in either the expected or opposite direction, but the evidence is too unstable and exploratory to support acceptance. I keep them deferred. Multiplicity is important: these are per-comparison 95% Welch intervals across a broad screen, and none would be compelling as a standalone discovery under stricter multiplicity control. No causal or generalizable claims are made. Independent validation is requested only for H16, the strongest and most focused lead.

Iteration 2/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: At synthesis, the new validation for H16 changes the interpretation. The independent interval R25 has signed estimate -0.0349 for a positive-direction H16 hypothesis, with lower and upper bounds -0.1061 and 0.0363; the original discovery R13 was -0.0327, with interval -0.0817 to 0.0163. Using approximately 10 percent of the absolute outcome_006 mean as the clinically meaningful threshold, about 0.0175, the validation point is beyond threshold but in the opposite direction from the registered positive claim, and the interval includes null, clinically meaningful negative effects, and clinically meaningful positive effects. Thus the high-feature_051 component of the prior H10 interaction lead is not supported and cannot be accepted. I leave H16 unresolved but close it, and also close the mirror H34, the H10 interaction lead, and complementary H33; this is an insufficient-precision exploratory pathway, not proof of absence. The remaining dataset-supported conclusions are still negative or equivalence-style findings: for outcome_001, feature_034 and feature_002 contrasts are entirely inside the approximately 0.0415 clinical threshold, and for outcome_013 feature_002 is inside the approximately 0.0269 threshold, so those exact tested contrasts support rejection of clinically meaningful differences. No positive or negative association is accepted. Several weak leads are deferred: feature_054 level_001 versus level_002 had raw negative contrasts on outcome_001 and outcome_011 but below clinical margins and including zero; outcome_013 feature_034 raw positive is below threshold and imprecise; prior feature_060 contrasts and other low-priority screens remain deferred. The most informative next analysis is a high-power main-effect screen of the balanced predictors feature_034, feature_002, and feature_060 on untested outcomes with similar favorable clinical margins, plus one new high-prevalence predictor feature_047 on outcome_001 and outcome_011. New claims are registered with direction -1 so a positive signed estimate corresponds to raw exposed-minus-comparator negative, i.e. stronger dependency. Acceptance will require a signed point beyond the outcome-specific clinical margin and an interval substantially excluding null and the opposite direction; equivalence rejection will require an interval inside the clinical margin. Independent validation should be used only after such a discovery appears, and any accepted result remains a dataset association, not causal or generalizable.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: I appraised the 12 newly delivered discovery results. I continued to use an approximate clinically meaningful scale equal to about 10% of the absolute outcome mean, because these dependency-score means are negative and a signed relative interpretation is ambiguous; typical margins are about 0.025 for most tested outcomes, about 0.027 for outcome_013, and about 0.028 for outcome_008. Estimates are already signed to the claim direction, so a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is negative, i.e. stronger dependency in the exposed group. No new result meets the acceptance standard: no interval excludes zero while the point estimate is beyond the approximate clinical margin and the interval also excludes the opposite clinical direction. Several results are clean equivalence-style nulls. H51, H54, H56, and H39 have intervals entirely inside the approximate clinical margins, so I reject clinically meaningful differences for those exact tested contrasts and close them. H57 is nearly equivalent but its lower signed bound lies slightly outside the negative margin, so I do not formally reject equivalence; the point is weak and opposite to the negative-direction hypothesis, so it remains unresolved and deferred. H53 and H57 similarly fail equivalence only because one bound is just beyond the margin; they are not accepted. H50, H52, and H55 have positive signed point estimates in the hypothesized stronger-dependency direction, but the points are below the clinical margin and the intervals include null while extending into clinically meaningful territory; they are unresolved and deferred. H38 has a signed negative point, meaning the raw contrast is positive/opposite, and the interval is mostly within margin but its lower signed bound just allows a clinically meaningful opposite raw effect; it remains unresolved and deferred because feature_034 still has untested follow-up screens. H58 and H59 are feature_054 follow-ups: their signed negative points correspond to raw positive contrasts, opposite to the earlier feature_054 raw negative leads on outcome_001 and outcome_011, and their intervals include null and clinically meaningful opposite raw effects while excluding a clinically meaningful negative-direction effect. Together with the earlier inconsistent feature_054 results, this gives no support for a robust feature_054 main-effect association, so I close H58 and H59 and also close the related H17/H20/H35/H36 feature_054 main-effect claims. Multiplicity is important: these were twelve per-comparison Welch discovery intervals, and even near-threshold interval boundaries should not be treated as standalone discoveries. Cell counts exceed the 20-observation requirement, and there is no obvious leakage or coding error, but these are unadjusted dataset associations and predictor correlations or confounding remain possible. I request no independent validation because none of the new results is a robust lead; the equivalence rejections are already supported by intervals inside the clinical margin, and validating weak near-zero signals is unlikely to be informative.
